correctness.rationale: Stationary flow is π_i r_i=J, so the reversed chain jumps counterclockwise out of i at the same rate r_i. Reflections i↦−i for b=d and i↦2−i for a=c conjugate the generators, preserve π and parity, and prove full reversibility on the two surfaces. In each alternating word three intervals change parity; only the one-jump paths contribute at order h³, giving JU and JV. Their difference is −J(a−c)(b−d), proving necessity. Stationary marginals of 00 and 11 force the only nonpalindromic length-three pairs to be equal. For length four I checked the prefix/suffix balance at 000, 111, 010, 101, 001 and 100: the five other signed differences are 0, 0, Δ, −Δ, Δ as ordered in RESULT.md. A word with m changes has probability Θ(h^m) because exactly the required jumps with all other intervals jump-free give a positive leading term. For nonalternating reversal pairs m≤2, so (p−q) log(p/q)=O(h^{6−m})=O(h⁴); the alternating pair gives the stated cubic coefficient with O(h⁴) remainder. Every word has positive probability at fixed h>0. The asymptotics are for fixed positive rates, and the minimality is only for equally spaced observations. The supplied script was inspected, not executed.

value.rationale: The motivating question is how much directional information remains in the shortest usable uniformly spaced record after parity hides the microscopic cycle. The exact leading KL quantifies that question, identifying the uncommon alternating records that carry the leading information and the dependence on both opposite-rate contrasts. This is not a microscopic dissipation estimate (the microscopic reversed paths lack support), nor an entropy rate. It is a concrete finite-window observable near a sharp reversibility boundary.
